title: Cap. VIII: Hactenus Jesuitarum — turn to Corvinus; negative reprobation to liberty alone
pass_a_gloss: Thus far we have ventilated the arguments of the Jesuits and of the Scholastics. Certain others also are urged by Corvinus, in the Defense of the Arminian sentence against Tilenus: in which if anything new occur, it shall be washed away. But so much the more must we labor, that we may recall the negative act of reprobation, which we can call passing by or non-election, unto the sole liberty of the Divine will, because all who deduce this reprobation from foresight of evil acts also suspend election from foresight of good acts.
pass_b_english: So far we have aired the Jesuits' and Scholastics' arguments. Corvinus also presses others in his Defense of the Arminian sentence against Tilenus — and if anything new appears there, it will be cleared. We must labor all the more to recall the negative act of reprobation — which we may call praeterition or non-election — to the sole liberty of the divine will. For all who derive this reprobation from foresight of evil acts also hang election on foresight of good acts.
source_text: Hactenus Jesuitarum ac Scholasticorum argumenta ventilavimus. Urgentur et alia nonnulla a Corvino, in Defensione sententiae Arminianae adversus Tilenum: in quibus si quid occurrat novi, diluetur. Eo autem magis nobis laborandum est, ut reprobationis actum negativum, quem praeteritionem sive non-electionem vocare possumus, ad solam Divinae voluntatis libertatem revocemus, quia omnes qui hanc reprobationem ex praevisione actuum malorum deducunt, electionem etiam ex praevisione actuum bonorum suspendunt.
